title: Column reflects on Sacred Heart devotion and the experience of parenthood
text:
Laura Kelly Fanucci, author and founder of Mothering Spirit, reflected on the connection between the devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus and the experience of parenthood in a column published on June 15. Fanucci referenced a quote from Elizabeth Stone: “Making the decision to have a child — it is momentous. It is to decide forever to have your heart go walking around outside your body.” She said this sentiment captures the vulnerability, anxiety, lack of control, and love that comes with raising children.
Fanucci drew parallels between parental love and Christ’s sacrifice as depicted in Sacred Heart imagery. She wrote, “Christ is shown holding his own heart, pointing to a human heart pierced with thorns, held in his wounded hands, giving his whole self to us in the most visceral way.” According to Fanucci, parents share in this type of love: “What is the holy beat of the Sacred Heart if not the same joyful, painful throb that parents feel… knowing they will forever have their whole heart walking around outside their body?”
She described encounters with parents who shared stories involving grief or hardship but also resilience and hope. Fanucci said she has witnessed “the resilience and radical love of parents who come to understand that while they cannot control or change their children, they can always come to God with every hope that Love will carry their children through whatever life brings.”
Fanucci recounted her own experiences as a parent facing loss and pain but found comfort in reflecting on Christ’s willingness not to shield himself from suffering: “The Sacred Heart reminds me that nothing — not even the bruised or broken parts of our lives — needs to be hidden from God.” She quoted St. Margaret Mary Alacoque describing God’s heart as an abyss offering joy and mercy.
The column concluded by urging readers not only to contemplate but also be changed by images of sacrificial love: “You cannot see a bleeding heart and turn away unchanged.” Fanucci wrote that both God and parents allow their hearts out into the world for others.
